title: Random Forests
summary: Leo Breiman published "Random Forests" in Machine Learning in October 2001. The paper describes random forests as combinations of tree predictors in which each tree depends on a randomly sampled vector, and analyzes forest generalization error in terms of individual-tree strength and correlation.
significance: A documented machine-learning milestone for random-forest ensemble methods, recorded from the original Springer publisher record and a University of California, Berkeley technical-report record documenting Breiman's closely related earlier random-forest work.

verification.note: Springer records the Machine Learning article as issue date October 2001, volume 45, pages 5-32, DOI 10.1023/A:1010933404324. UC Berkeley separately preserves Breiman's 1999 technical report "Random Forests--Random Features". LINEAiGE records only the October 2001 journal-publication milestone here and does not infer a universal invention date, geography, ancestry, influence, causality, or relationships.
